object: Langen Foundation — empty passage between concrete volume and glass enclosure
creator: Tadao Ando
branch: Contemporary reductive architectural space; serial frames, planar wall and active passage void
attribution: Till Niermann, Langen Foundation 3, 2021.jpg, photographed 19 June 2021, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0. Exact provider 1280px thumbnail; no local crop or retouch.
rights_evidence: The exact Commons file/API record names Till Niermann, identifies the building by Tadao Ando in Neuss, dates the photograph 19 June 2021 and specifies CC BY 3.0. The photo license does not automatically clear all depicted architecture rights or every use.
claim_scope: A scoped example of contemporary architectural reduction: uninterrupted wall, repeated thin frames and the intervening passage govern the visible space. Not an original Minimal Art work or an exclusive distinction from Modernism.
limits: One empty passage between the glass skin and concrete volume, not a complete building exterior, floor plan, or whole exhibition. The far-end green exit sign and small fire-safety fixture remain but are minor, normal functional elements. Natural outdoor views, surface marks and strong frame shadows remain. Do not infer all hidden structure or claim this is 1960s American Minimal Art. Architectural reduction overlaps broader Modernism; the complementary Judd image supplies a separate historical Minimal Art branch.
observable_features: A continuous plain concrete wall runs beside a transparent outer wall and glazed roof, leaving a long empty passage between them.
Repeated slender vertical and overhead members establish a regular progression toward a small far opening.
Strong linear frame shadows fall across the uncluttered floor and glass, making intervals and perspective depth easy to inspect.
The main view contains no visitors, display sculptures, furniture groupings or foreground tree branches; attention rests on wall, frame, gap and light relationships.

association_evidence.supports: The exact Commons record identifies this view as Langen Foundation, Tadao Ando’s building in Neuss, and provides Till Niermann’s photograph date and CC BY 3.0 license.

The institution documents the 2004 opening, concrete/glass/steel composition, elongated concrete volume veiled in glass, and Ando’s geometric austerity. The selected passage photograph illustrates a partial visible reduction; the institution does not certify it as a 1960s Minimal Art work.
